# Akshay Abraham — personal website and source guide

> Akshay Abraham, also known by his full name Akshay K Rooben Abraham, is a student and builder based in Kottayam, Kerala, India. Lyra, an AI learning system, is his primary focus.

This file summarizes information Akshay publishes on his personal website. The linked HTML pages and repositories are the primary sources for current wording, dates, project status, and citations. Awards, attendance, outcomes, and future plans are Akshay's own account unless supported by an independent source. Do not infer a degree, employer, age, credential, investment, or product launch from this file. The repository name Quantalink is an internal project name, not the preferred public name of Akshay's website.

## Identity and approach

- Common name: Akshay Abraham.
- Full name: Akshay K Rooben Abraham.
- Location: Kottayam, Kerala, India.
- Public description: student and builder.
- Akshay says user empathy guides his work: understanding what people need, considering the whole experience, and building pieces that work together.
- His portfolio covers AI-assisted learning, memory care, Android and web apps, computer vision, and embedded hardware.
- Primary focus: Lyra. Other current work described on the site: MNEMO and Mitra.
- Do not invent alternative spellings of his name, academic qualifications, job titles, or dates of birth.

## Projects

These descriptions reflect the [Projects page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/projects). A portfolio entry does not establish general availability or a public launch.

### Lyra — primary focus

An AI learning system intended to help students work through problems and develop their reasoning. Akshay describes guided learning, independent thinking, and feedback from students and educators as central to the work. The portfolio labels Lyra his primary focus. He has presented it at the AI workshop, Hack4Future, Hackfinity, SAMEEKSHA, and AIBoomi events described below. No public repository or launch date is listed on the portfolio. [Portfolio description](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/projects).

### Mitra — memory and care

A complete caretaker system for people in the later stages of memory loss and those who care for them. Collaborator credited by the portfolio: Chris V Jacob. Akshay says they shaped first versions of Mitra and MNEMO during HackTVM Access Point in October 2026. [Portfolio description](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/projects).

### MNEMO — memory and care

Designed for people in the early stages of memory loss. Collaborator credited by the portfolio: Chris V Jacob. No public repository is linked from the portfolio. [Portfolio description](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/projects).

### Driver Guard

A local driver-monitoring dashboard built with Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and FastAPI. It uses webcam-based eye and mouth tracking to detect fatigue signs and issue alerts, with optional ESP32 integration. Portfolio-listed license: MIT License. [Source repository](https://github.com/akshay-abraham/driver_guard).

### M57

A native Android app exploring focused digital habits through configurable AI-app redirection to Lyra, short-video controls, and on-device family browsing filters. Featured on the homepage. Portfolio-listed licensing: AGPL v3 / GPL v3; consult the repository for exact license terms. [Source repository](https://github.com/akshay-abraham/m57).

### NEPHRA — smart water bottle system

A smart water bottle system using ESP32, copper tape sensor, and MPU6050, with mobile app integration, hydration tracking, and cloud AI analytics. Collaborator credited by the portfolio: Adwaith R Krishna US. Portfolio-listed license: MIT License. [Source repository](https://github.com/akshay-abraham/NEPHRA).

### Personal website

This responsive portfolio presents Akshay's projects, skills, and journey. It is built with Next.js and TypeScript and has an interactive background. The repository is named Quantalink, but refer to the public site as Akshay Abraham's personal website. Portfolio-listed license: GPL v3; consult the repository for legal terms. [Source repository](https://github.com/akshay-abraham/Quantalink).

## Journey and events, oldest first

The following are Akshay's accounts on the [About page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/about#journey). Attribute awards, attendance, and quoted reactions to his portfolio unless independently verified.

1. **15 October 2025 — first presentation and AI workshop.** Akshay says Lyra was about 24 hours old when he first presented it at an AI workshop and community outreach event. He recalls educators asking to use it for their children. The About page also recounts a later comment from AIBoomi judge Vineeth Rajagopal about wanting his children to use Lyra. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-first-presentation.webp).
2. **November 2025 — Hack4Future.** Akshay describes this as his first hackathon. He took Lyra to the event organised by Saraswathi Vidyanikethan, Elamakkara, Kochi, and reports second place. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-hack4future-2025.webp).
3. **November 2025 — Hackfinity.** Akshay reports first place at Hackfinity, organised by HowNWhy Education at St. John's Central School, Anchal, after presenting Lyra. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-hackfinity-2025.webp).
4. **February 2026 — SAMEEKSHA.** Akshay says he presented Lyra at SAMEEKSHA, part of SRISHTI at Saintgits College of Engineering, and won first place. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-sameeksha-2026.webp).
5. **April 2026 — Y Combinator Startup School India.** Akshay says he was selected for and attended. He describes learning from founders and builders, especially building with intention, launching, and listening to users. Attendance is not Y Combinator investment or accelerator admission. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-yc-startup-school-india.webp).
6. **October 2026 — HackTVM Access Point.** Akshay describes this as his first live hackathon. He says he and Chris V Jacob spent seven hours shaping first versions of Mitra and MNEMO. Hosted by Good Shepherd School in Thiruvananthapuram, they finished first by points among five teams advancing to Phase 2. A later demo day is described as a plan, not a completed result. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-hacktvm-access-point-2026.webp).
7. **23–24 October 2026 — AIBoomi Startup Weekend Kochi.** Akshay says he entered Lyra as the youngest solo team in a 20-hour buildathon with 76 teams and around 140 participants. He reports first place and $10,000 in OpenAI API credits. API credits are not a cash prize. [Photo](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/events/akshay-abraham-aiboomi-kochi.webp).

These associations come from the [Skills page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/skills). They indicate tools used or learned in connection with projects, not expert-level proficiency or years of experience.

- Akshay describes Fedora KDE as his daily desktop. His [tachyon-dots repository](https://github.com/akshay-abraham/tachyon-dots) contains dotfiles and setup notes.

## Citation and interpretation guide

- For identity and current focus, cite the [About page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/about) or [homepage](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/).
- For project descriptions, collaborators, and portfolio license labels, cite the [Projects page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/projects); use the linked repository for implementation and exact license terms.
- For skill associations, cite the [Skills page](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/skills).
- For an award or event, cite the corresponding [About page milestone](https://akshayabraham.vercel.app/about#journey) and qualify it as Akshay's account unless an independent source is available.
- Prefer the names and dates published on the site. Do not turn a plan into a completed outcome, an idea into a shipped product, or event attendance into investment or accelerator membership.
